description: Print through out() from bin/lib/output-sink.ts, never straight to the process's stdout. That rules out process.stdout.write; every console method but warn, error, trace and assert (log, info, debug, dir, dirxml, table, count, group, groupCollapsed, timeLog, timeEnd … all print to stdout), also through globalThis; the process.stdout stream handed around as a value (`(ok ? process.stdout : process.stderr).write(…)`, `output: process.stdout`); the stream taken out of process under another name (`import { stdout } from 'node:process'`, `const { stdout: s } = process`); and process or console itself taken under another name or passed as a value (`const p = process; p.stdout.write(…)`, `f(console)`, `{ io: process }`, `const { log } = console`, `const { ...all } = process`), which would hide either from the member checks. Reading process.stdout.isTTY / columns / rows is fine. The MCP server runs the same verbs in-process (pensmith_plan / pensmith_write / pensmith_verify) and speaks JSON-RPC on stdout, so it points the sink at stderr before it connects, and pensmith_status captures it with withCapturedOutput(); a direct write would corrupt the frame (T1-15). The CLI keeps the default sink, the process's stdout, so its output is byte-identical. bin/lib/pdf-worker.ts is exempt: it runs in a worker thread whose console goes to the worker's own captured stream, which pdf-text.ts never forwards (SEC-02). The hook entries in hooks/ are out of scope: their stdout is the hook protocol.
